findings.quote: | "one service for VPCs with the same CIDR" | an endpoint service | VPCs [can have overlapping IP address ranges](../facts/privatelink.md#privatelink-wp-consumer-and-provider-may-overlap) | both sides start connections: renumber, then peering |
findings.evidence: The 'But not if' guard has no fact and points to the wrong answer. The chapter's own verified question vpc-connectivity-q011 (same CIDR block, the provider must also start connections) keys a second, reversed endpoint service, citing fact privatelink-endpoint-service-needs-load-balancer, and its distractor d cites fact vpc-private-nat-allow-listed-and-overlapping ('enable communication between networks even if they have overlapping CIDR ranges'). No saved page recommends renumbering as the answer. A reader who trusts this guard picks re-addressing plus peering on a q011-style stem. Replace the guard with 'the other side must also start connections: a second endpoint service in the other direction', or drop it.

findings.quote: | [$0.01/GB in both "In" and "Out" direction](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-cross-az-data-transfer-price) | Peering traffic between zones | Busy peers belong in one zone |
findings.evidence: The 'Why it decides an answer' cell gives a design rule with no fact, and it pushes toward a single-AZ placement that the book's resilience questions mark wrong (the chapter's own q009 keys 'the design must stay in three Availability Zones'; fact vpc-endpoints-interface-two-azs-for-production: 'at least two Availability Zones per VPC endpoint'). The fact behind the cost is vpc-peering-guide-pricing-no-creation-charge-free-in-az: 'All data transfer over a VPC peering connection that stays within an Availability Zone is free, even if it's between different accounts. Charges apply for data transfer over VPC peering connections that cross Availability Zones and Regions.' Write the cell as that cost rule (same zone free, across zones charged) and let the stem's resilience requirement decide.

findings.quote: | What you pay | [Data transfer across peering connections is charged](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-faq-no-creation-charge) | Hourly: the [connections that you make to the Transit Gateway](../facts/transit-gateway.md#transit-gateway-pricing-hourly-attachment-and-data-processing), plus traffic | Endpoint hours [provisioned in each Availability Zone](../facts/privatelink.md#privatelink-faq-billing-interface-gwlb-hourly-per-az) |
findings.evidence: Bullet 4.4.S3 ('Configuring appropriate network routes to minimize network transfer costs') is tested by q012 (move a 40 TB pair from the transit gateway to peering), but neither file states the mechanism that decides it: fact transit-gateway-pricing-data-processing-per-gb-sent-to-gateway ('Data processing charges apply for each gigabyte sent from a VPC, Direct Connect or VPN or Network Firewall to the AWS Transit Gateway') against fact vpc-peering-guide-pricing-no-creation-charge-free-in-az (peering: no creation charge, free inside one Availability Zone, charged across zones). As written, the cost row reads 'all three cost something'. Make the row say: peering, no hourly or processing charge, transfer charged only across zones; transit gateway, per attachment hour plus per GB processed.

findings.quote: The 40 TB then flows over the peering connection instead of the transit gateway, and there is [no charge for creating VPC peering connections](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-faq-no-creation-charge).
findings.evidence: The why of the correct option a gives a reason that does not decide the question: a one-time creation charge is irrelevant to a 40 TB monthly bill. The deciding fact is transit-gateway-pricing-data-processing-per-gb-sent-to-gateway ('Data processing charges apply for each gigabyte sent from a VPC ... to the AWS Transit Gateway'), which peering does not have (vpc-peering-guide-pricing-no-creation-charge-free-in-az). The explanation also never says this; it relies on 'lowest overall cost'. Rewrite the why with the per-GB processing fact, so the question teaches the 4.4.S3 mechanism (stem, options and key unchanged).

findings.quote: If the stem said "the company must manage all VPC routing in one place" instead: keep the analytics pair on the transit gateway, because peering adds routes outside the hub.

findings.quote: | "heavy S3 traffic through a NAT gateway" | a gateway endpoint | [Gateway VPC endpoints have no hourly charges](../facts/vpc-endpoints.md#vpc-endpoints-wa-cost08-gateway-free-interface-hourly) | the data center sends it: an interface endpoint |
findings.evidence: The guard cannot co-occur with the signal: traffic from the data center does not pass through the VPC's NAT gateway, so a stem with this signal never meets this guard. The guard that does flip the answer on a NAT-cost stem is the bucket's Region: fact vpc-endpoints-gateway-region-only ('A gateway endpoint is available only in the Region where you created it. Be sure to create your gateway endpoint in the same Region as your S3 buckets.'). Use 'the bucket is in another Region' as the guard; the data-center case already has its own row 5.

findings.quote: For a gateway endpoint the [Principal element must be set to](../facts/vpc-endpoints.md#vpc-endpoints-policy-gateway-principal-star-use-principalarn) the wildcard, and naming the role would still give it no allow.
findings.evidence: The deep subsection says only 'It [must contain a Principal element]' and never teaches the gateway-endpoint rule of fact vpc-endpoints-policy-gateway-principal-star-use-principalarn; only task t03 (pass_route false) states it ('A gateway endpoint policy keeps Principal * and names principals in a Condition'). A pass-route reader meets the rule first in a distractor rationale. Add half a sentence to step 2 of the endpoint-policy subsection.

findings.quote: **Decision.** An endpoint service behind a Network Load Balancer. Peering fails: you [cannot create a VPC peering connection](../facts/vpc-peering.md#vpc-peering-no-overlap-ipv4-ipv6) between overlapping blocks.
findings.evidence: The requirement asks 'Which design is the MOST secure?', but the decision removes both other options only because they cannot work with overlapping blocks; the security reason (one service, one direction, an allow list of accounts: facts privatelink-wp-only-consumer-initiates and privatelink-endpoint-service-not-available-by-default) is not in the Decision line. This models the habit of answering a qualifier question by feasibility alone. Lint W201 also reports 'Decision record has 210 words; the section allows 0 to 150', so trimming and adding the security clause go together.
